title: As Above, So Below
coverDescription: Marcelo Sanchez - Art for cover and interior
description: In a time beyond Ragnarök, Zeus in his disenchantment with mankind, sends a purge of fire to Earth.  Cupid overhears the commotion at Mount Olympus and sends an arrow of love to change his heart and tragically crumples the god to rubble.  Medusa seizes the opportunity and ascends to the throne because of Zeus’ misfortune.  Cupid escapes with the Scepter of Zeus into a portal.  With the unbalance of good and evil unleashed in the Cosmos, Hell spills out onto Earth, and the Tree of Life lays, dying.  The Cosmic Kraken, Chaos, is set loose to destroy all life and life while his berserker, Manafest is set free to do his bidding.  The Fates of Destiny scramble to fend off the evil and in times of peril they bestow their combined powers of Premonition on those tied to their fate.  So, the Yogen is born.
synopsis:
The Story

In a time beyond Ragnarok, God is dead, consumed by His hatred for mankind. Cracks form across the cosmic egg of creation.  The Tree of Life, which grants life to all, slowly withers away. The immortals begin falling one by one.  CHAOS, the Child of Darkness, looms, threatening to engulf all life and light and plunge everything into nothingness. Both Heaven and Hell have lost sovereignty, and evil spills out upon Earth. Desperation befalls the gods as they face extinction.  Zeus, disillusioned with humanity, had unleashed a purge of fire upon the Earth before his demise, Premonition’s first test. 

The Fates of Destiny arrive at the birth of the baby boy, weaving their fate upon him only to realize his fate has already been woven with their own. When the time is right, they will return to finish their web, thereby sealing his fate. In the meantime, Chance, lives out his life in tragedy, unbeknownst of his life to come. He lives a privileged life until one day it all comes crashing down with the death of his true love and unborn child. Consumed by anger and grief, he seeks vengeance and, unintentionally, takes the life of the perpetrator, leading to his imprisonment. He becomes an old and broken man.  Yearning to be reunited with his lost loves in the afterlife; he decides to end his life by jumping from a cliff.  At that moment, the Fates of Destiny appear with an intriguing proposition: if he agrees to assist them in the battle against the evil that plagues the Cosmos, they will reset his timeline and thereby finish their Web of Fate.   

In a long succession of heroes, the Premonition power awakens across time when the Cosmos needs them most.  The source of the power comes from the Tree of Life and is bestowed by the combined powers of the weavers of fate, the guardians of the Tree of Life. These sisters are seers of the past, present, and future and weave one’s fate at the time of their birth.  Rayvn is the weaver of fate.  Decima measures the length of the thread of one’s life or timeline.  Morta cuts the thread thereby sealing one’s fate.  

Across the cosmos, the former champion known as Premonition Omicron, has fallen. Finally defeated by henchman of Chaos, Manafest.  Premonition is defeated with the aid of Decima, the Fate of the Present, who has forsaken her sisters to join the fight against good. With Medusa at the throne, Decima is promised a place in her dominion, leading to internal strife among the Fates of Destiny as they clash with Manafest. 

With the death of Omicron, the Premonition power escapes into the Cosmos and takes with it the Fates of Destiny, who now bestow their combined powers onto Chance, and a new hero is born. He age-regresses to his younger self, becoming immortal–with one catch: his memory is lost, all but for his love.  Chance grapples with a profound identity crisis, haunted by his true nature and lost love all while trying to learn his new powers, all in an effort, to stop the purge of fire from engulfing the planet. Throughout this quest to reclaim his memories and understand his purpose, the Fates of Destiny reappear at different junctures, offering assistance and guidance to our reluctant hero. 

Chance first finds solace in a gifted psychic, a descendant of the Oracle of Delphi, with the ability to commune with the dead and glimpse into realms beyond even Premonition's reach. This psychic becomes an essential ally, helping Chance comprehend the extent of his powers and aid him in his quest for self-discovery.  He is later catapulted into the past with a misstep in his initial battle with Manafest into a time of the Vikings, where he learns how to fight and wield his powers with the help of his inner light.  

Premonition later returns to the present after mastering his power and confronts Manafest and the purge of fire.  Other challenges arise.  The fifth dimension is also threatened with the collapse of the third dimension and sends a champion to combat CHAOS.  Later tricked by Manafest, our hero's heart is tainted by darkness, and he joins evils cause.  Morta, the Fate of the Future, escapes to the Gates of Hades and traverses the underworld to resurrect Premonition Alpha to combat the newfound evil Premonition, Dark Heart. Over several battles, our hero's goodness is restored, allowing him to vanquish Manafest and other sworn foes summoned to defeat him. 

This truly is a love story.  In the end, Premonition confronts CHAOS while fighting for his love.  Witnessing the hero's unwavering devotion, Zeus regains faith in and love for humanity which breaks Him free from Cupid’s spell, that had turned him into stone. With renewed vigor, Zeus joins the battle, helping to subdue Chaos and reinstates the delicate balance between light and darkness. Chance is returned to his former life, before the tragic accident that claimed his wife and child, while still retaining the Power of Premonition, that he employs to prevent the catastrophe. 

Throughout the story, Chance grapples with internal struggles between darkness and light, and external conflicts that challenge his resolve. Despite his increasing power, it is not mere strength that triumphs over darkness, but rather the hero's unwavering selfless love that ultimately saves the Cosmos as well as his soul and the lives of his loved ones.  At the end there is a twist where it appears this was all in Chance’s mind, as he lay dying, in the same car crash his wife and child die.  But his wife survives, and it is their son that becomes the next Premonition.  Throughout the story there is many villains and side quests and lesser-known mythological characters interwoven in the story.
artist: Art by Marcelo Sanchez. Colors by Vittorio Sanchez

title: A Pictorial History of Classic Nurse Paperback Covers
description:
The 1960s and 1970s witnessed upheavals in American culture, an explosion of new ideas in cinema; a renaissance in American abstract painting, and, yes, lots of semi-salacious, suggestive, and down right kitschy “Nurse Paperbacks” which boasted covers which were eye-catching and enticing. Each of these covers are little gems that present images which reeled readers in. This book chronicles these covers and presents the first pictorial history of classic “nurse” paperback covers and features an in-depth essay about the genre and profiles many of the artists involved in creating the artwork for these tomes.
Each of these covers showcase a different aspect of the genre and were created by some of the finest illustrators of the era. Each cover, many reproduced from the original paintings, show the tongue in check humor employed in the creation these pop-culturally iconic covers.

title: MANDRAKE THE MAGICIAN HC VOL 05 THE COMPLETE NEWSPAPER DAILIES
seriesName: Mandrake the Magician: The Complete Newspaper Dailies
description:
"Mandrake the Magician began as a daily strip on June 11, 1934, and whether Lee Falk knew it as a sophomore at the University of Illinois, he was making history. The daily strip ended after a 79-year run, and the Sunday strip, which started in 1935, ran for 68 years. Any fan of comic strips is almost certainly familiar with Falk’s other creation, The Phantom, which started in 1936 and continues to this day.
The strips presented in this series of reprints feature two staple characters in addition to the master magician: Lothar and Princess Narda (princess of the mythical European kingdom Cockaigne). Lothar appears within the first few days (June 14, 1934), and Narda is introduced in Mandrake’s second adventure. Narda is similar to Flash Gordon’s Dale Arden: beautiful, constantly in need of rescue, and the love interest of our hero. A Prince of the Seven Nations of Africa, Lothar is Mandrake’s devoted servant, friend and companion. He is, “the strongest man in the world,” and decked out in a fez, shorts, and a leopard shirt.
Comics historian Don Markstein commented that, “Some people say Mandrake the Magician...was comics’ first superhero,” and we at Hermes Press couldn’t agree more. Volume five presents: “The Mystery of the Striped Orchid,” 4/7/1941 - 6/21/1941; “The Great Grando,” 6/23/1941 - 11/8/194; “Lothar The Champ,” 11/10/1941 - 7/11/194; “The Rumor Factory,” 7/13/1942 - 9/12/194; and “Baron Kord,” 9/14/1942 - 4/10/1943."

It's the Swingin' Sixties, a time of the Cold War, evil criminal organizations and super spies.  Enter three special ladies: Patty, Coco and Martine.  Most know them as workers at the international Jet Setters Club, but they are secretly of part the agency known as B.U.N.N.Y.  They must leap into action to stop a plot to destroy the Vatican!
